text:
The Apatanis who inhabit a tranquil pine clad valley called Ziro at the core of Lower Subansiri District of Arunachal Pradesh, are famous for their unique practice of wet rice cultivation. They are also known for their sustainable agricultural practices and the agricultural cycles govern their everyday lives. The agricultural festival of Dree is the highlight in this cycle.

--- Practical Travel Context (Wikivoyage) ---
Ziro, also spelt Zero, is a picturesque town in Arunachal Pradesh, India. It is known for a four-season tourist place and gives a pleasant feel in every season with variant colours in different seasons. It is included the Tentative List for UNESCO's World Heritage Site for the Apatani cultural landscape.
best_time: March to June (pleasant summer flowers) and September to November (crisp autumn views)
